chunks: Ali narrated from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughirah, from Muawiya ibn Maytharah, that Sinan asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who extends one of his legs in front of him while he is sitting, and he said:
"There is no harm, and I do not see it [as specific to this posture] except for the convalescent or the sick."

key_terms.الْمُعْتَلِّ: The convalescent / one recovering from illness
key_terms.لاَ بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on extending one leg while sitting in prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the prayer of the compelled (*al-Mudtir*), this hadith clarifies that extending one leg while sitting is not only permissible but characteristic of the ill (*al-Mu'tall*), thereby validating natural postures during prayer without requiring strict uniformity. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (*rukhas*) for those with physical limitations, distinguishing between ritual obligation and natural bodily comfort. It reflects the broader Imami tradition of accommodating human frailty in acts of worship, ensuring that the validity of prayer is not compromised by minor deviations caused by illness or age.
